resources.string: Prevents turning off the website filter while it is locked. It closes the Settings screens that would deactivate uninstall protection, disconnect or forget the filter VPN, or turn off this guard. It reads only the Settings app and nothing else.
No websites blocked yet. Subdomains are blocked too (facebook.com also blocks www.facebook.com and m.facebook.com).
That doesn\'t look like a website address
Set random password (you won\'t know it)
Locked. You need the password to stop the filter, remove websites or turn off protection. Adding websites is always allowed.
No password set. Anyone can stop the filter and the protection does nothing.

Uninstall protection makes the app a device admin, so it can't be uninstalled, force stopped or have its data cleared.

The Settings guard closes the screens that would deactivate the device admin, disconnect the VPN or turn off the guard itself.

On Android 13+ you may first need to open App info for Blocker, tap ⋮ and choose "Allow restricted settings" before the guard can be enabled.
This stops Blocker from being uninstalled while the filter is locked. To uninstall, unlock with your password or with the emergency code.

If you forgot the password (or set a random one), you can unlock everything with the long emergency code. It is shown on a separate screen. Copy, paste and screenshots are disabled, so you have to write it on paper and type it back in.
Filter: should run but is stopped. Tap \"Start filter\".
A long random password will be set and never shown to anyone. After that, the only way to stop the filter or uninstall the app is the emergency code.
Random password set. Only the emergency code can unlock it now.
Tap to turn it back on
Blocker is locked. Unlock it in the app first.
Blocker is locked. Unlock it with the password or the emergency code inside the app first.
Write this code on paper. Then go back, tap \"Enter emergency code\" and type it in exactly. Upper and lower case matter, spaces don\'t. The code never uses 0, O, o, 1, l or I.
Type the emergency code you wrote on paper. Pasting is disabled. Entering the correct code removes the password, stops the filter and turns off uninstall protection, so you can uninstall the app.
The code is wrong. Check it for typos.
The password was removed, the filter was stopped and uninstall protection was turned off. You can now uninstall Blocker or turn off the Settings guard.
This screen isn\'t available on your phone. Look for it in Settings.

Blocker blocks websites you don't want to visit, in every browser and app.

It already blocks well-known adult sites, YouTube and X. You can add more in the app.

Everything happens on your phone. Nothing is sent anywhere, and there are no ads and no accounts.

These cards walk you through the setup. Swipe or tap Next. You can open them again any time with the Help button.

Android will ask you to allow a VPN connection.

Blocker's VPN runs only on your phone. It checks the names of the websites your apps look up and stops the blocked ones. Page content, passwords and messages never pass through it.

While the filter runs, Android shows a key icon in the status bar.

Android requires apps that keep running in the background to show a notification. Blocker\'s notification is empty, and you can turn it off completely. The filter keeps running.\n\nOn the screen that opens, switch off notifications for Blocker.
Let it run in the background
Some phones stop background apps to save battery, and that would stop the filter too. Allow Blocker to run without battery restrictions.
In the list, find Blocker and choose \"Don\'t optimize\" or \"Unrestricted\".
On Xiaomi phones:\n• In App info, open Battery saver and choose \"No restrictions\".\n• Turn on Autostart for Blocker. Without it, the filter can\'t start after a restart.

Turn on "Always-on VPN" for Blocker. Android then starts the filter as soon as the phone starts.

On the screen that opens, tap ⚙ next to Blocker and switch on "Always-on VPN".

⚠ Leave "Block connections without VPN" OFF. Blocker's VPN only checks website names, so with that option on, no internet works at all.

Make Blocker a device admin. While it is one, Android won\'t let anyone uninstall Blocker, force stop it or clear its data.\n\nBlocker doesn\'t use any device admin powers. It can\'t lock, wipe or change your phone.

While Blocker is locked, the guard stops you from switching the protection off in Settings. It closes only these screens: deactivating the device admin, uninstalling Blocker, Blocker's VPN settings and the guard's own accessibility page.

The guard uses Android's accessibility feature. It looks only at the Settings app, and it doesn't read, store or send anything else.

On the screen that opens, find "Blocker Guard" (it may be under "Downloaded apps" or "Installed apps") and turn it on.
If Android says \"Restricted setting\": come back here, tap App info, tap ⋮ in the top-right corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\" and try again.

Do this last. Once Blocker is locked, the guard won't let you open the settings from the previous steps.

In the app, tap "Set password". From then on, stopping the filter, removing websites or turning off the protection needs the password.

Want to be really strict? Tap "Set random password" instead. That sets a long password nobody knows.

There is always a way back: the app shows a long emergency code. You can't copy it, so you have to write it on paper and type it back in. That's on purpose, so unlocking takes real effort.
⚠ \"Block connections without VPN\" is on, so no internet works. Tap here, open ⚙ next to Blocker and switch it off. Leave \"Always-on VPN\" on.
